reviews.reasoning: Re-derived from source bytes rather than trusting the row. Ps 50 is an identity psalm (the title sits inside MT v1), so the dual-cite web:Ps.50.0 = oshb:Ps.50.1 is arithmetically correct. MT 50:1 opens אֵ֤ל אֱֽלֹהִ֡ים יְֽהוָ֗ה (El, Elohim, YHWH) immediately before the verb of speech, byte-collated exactly as quoted; the 'before any verb of speech' framing holds. Selah at 50:6 is used correctly as corroboration only, not a driver. The seam at 50:6|50:7 is a strong, independently checkable register shift (third-person theophany narration to first-person divine self-address opening the next span), and the rejected_alternative correctly isolates that shift as the reason 50:7-9 was not folded in. High confidence is justified by how sharply both this row's own boundaries are marked. Observation, not a challenge: 'opening Book II's run of Asaph psalms' is loose phrasing (per the device inventory, le-Asaph = {50,73-83}; Book II carries only Ps 50, the eleven-psalm run sits in Book III) but survives a charitable reading ('opens the run, the first member falling in Book II') so no challenge is filed.

The closing self-identification formula אֱלֹהִ֖ים אֱלֹהֶ֣יךָ אָנֹֽכִי and the opening imperative both byte-collate exactly at oshb:Ps.50.7 as quoted. Re-reading the whole span, the '2 divine speeches' count holds: two sustained first-person discourse blocks (50:7-15 to 'my people', 50:16-23 to 'the wicked'), distinct from the single embedded quotation at 50:5 inside the third-person theophany; the count-object is used consistently with the sibling row. The rejected internal split at 50:10-12 is correct to call that anaphoric 'mine' sequence rhetorical elaboration rather than an addressee or frame change -- no competing tier-1 signal was found inside the span. The 50:23 cross-reference in device_notes checks out: 'the sacrifice of thanksgiving' recurs verbatim in WEB at both 50:14 and 50:23, a genuine inclusio. Confidence medium is a defensible, non-reflexive call: although both outer boundaries carry unusually strong explicit speech-frame formulas, the span's internal register (sacrifice polemic vs. positive instruction) is heterogeneous enough to withhold high confidence.

The dixit formula וְלָ֤רָשָׁ֨ע אָ֘מַ֤ר אֱלֹהִ֗ים opening MT 50:16 byte-collates exactly; it is the strongest addressee-shift marker available in the psalm and rightly grounds high confidence. WEB 50:22 and 50:23 quote verbatim against source. The inclusio claim (sacrifice-of-thanksgiving language at 50:14/50:23) independently checks out and is correctly treated as internal texture, not a boundary driver on its own. The rejected split at 50:22-23 is well-reasoned: appeal and accusation stay inside one uninterrupted address, so keeping them together is sound. No defects found in the quotes, the arithmetic, or the seam evidence.

The span and its front matter check out: the title dual-cite (web:Ps.51.0 = oshb:Ps.51.1 and = oshb:Ps.51.2) is arithmetically correct for this +2 psalm, and לְךָ֤ לְבַדְּךָ֨ חָטָאתִי֮ byte-collates exactly at oshb:Ps.51.6 (web:Ps.51.4 = oshb:Ps.51.6 is correct arithmetic). Keeping petition (51:1-2) and confession (51:3-6) as one strophe is defensible -- no vocative or speech-frame change occurs across the span -- and the rejected_alternative engages that rival fairly. The challenges below concern the row's philological/citation warrant, not the boundary itself.

challenges.claim: הֶ֭רֶב at MT 51:4 is glossed '(wash)' and treated as the root that recurs at 51:9, but it is not the wash-root.
challenges.evidence: MT 51:4 (oshb:Ps.51.4) reads הרבה הֶ֭רֶב כַּבְּסֵ֣נִי me'avoni umechatati taharani. הֶ֭רֶב is the qere of the ketiv הרבה, from the root r-b-h ('increase'), functioning as an adverbial intensifier ('greatly/thoroughly'); the wash-root is k-b-s, present in the same verse as כַּבְּסֵ֣נִי ('wash me') and genuinely recurring at 51:9 as תְּ֝כַבְּסֵ֗נִי (collate.py: byte tier at oshb:Ps.51.9). WEB's own rendering separates the two: 'Wash me thoroughly' = k-b-s (wash) + r-b-h (thoroughly). collate.py confirms הֶ֭רֶב is genuinely present at oshb:Ps.51.4 (byte tier), so the citation is not misplaced -- the gloss attached to it names the wrong lexeme.

challenges.claim: MT 51:4, quoted in this row's rationale, carries an undisclosed ketiv/qere note.
challenges.evidence: pmarks_Ps.json records kq=1 at Ps.51.4 (the ketiv/qere pair הרבה/הֶ֭רֶב itself); neither this row nor its sibling (M8-Ps-146, which also cites oshb:Ps.51.4 in its observed_substrate_signals) discloses the K/Q status of the verse despite quoting from it, though disclosure is required whenever a span quotes a K/Q verse (single-witness disclosure rule).

challenges.claim: device_notes' "this +2 psalm's rows dual-cite both MT title verses throughout" is a universal claim without an adjacent count, and checked against the cluster's own row set it risks overstating the pattern.
challenges.evidence: Of Psalm 51's four rows (145-148, confirmed exhaustive against freeze/cluster_map.json), only this opening row's boundary_evidence_refs carries the web:Ps.51.0 = oshb:Ps.51.1/2 title dual-cite; 146-148 correctly do not repeat it, per the owner rule that only a titled psalm's opening row carries the title reference. 'Throughout' is defensible under a charitable reading ('wherever the title is cited, both MT verses are given') but as written could be misread as 'every row'.

reviews.reasoning: The span itself is well supported: תְּ֝כַבְּסֵ֗נִי genuinely byte-collates at oshb:Ps.51.9 and is the true recurrence of the wash-root from 51:4 (see LF-146-2). The front seam (imperative cluster opening at 51:7) and back seam (cohortative vow opening at 51:13 -- אֲלַמְּדָ֣ה is a genuine 1cs cohortative, independently verified) are both well-marked register shifts, and no rival seam inside 51:7-12 was found strong enough to contest. High confidence for the span is reasonable given the density and clarity of the imperative cluster. The challenges below concern the row's own supporting citations, not the span.

challenges.claim: The Hebrew quoted as the counterpart of web:Ps.51.12 ('Restore to me the joy of your salvation. Uphold me with a willing spirit.') is not that verse's Hebrew -- it is the already-quoted Hebrew of web:Ps.51.10.
challenges.evidence: The row glosses לֵ֣ב טָ֭הוֹר בְּרָא ('a clean heart create for me') as '(oshb:Ps.51.12)' immediately after quoting web:Ps.51.12's English. But MT 51:12 is the counterpart of web:Ps.51.10 ('Create in me a clean heart...'), already quoted two clauses earlier in the same row; the true Hebrew of web:Ps.51.12 is oshb:Ps.51.14, הָשִׁ֣יבָה לִּ֭י שְׂשׂ֣וֹן יִשְׁעֶ֑ךָ וְר֖וּחַ נְדִיבָ֣ה תִסְמְכֵֽנִי ('restore to me the joy of your salvation, and a willing spirit sustain me'), sharing no vocabulary with the quoted line. collate.py confirms the quoted phrase collates at oshb:Ps.51.12 (tier=byte) and fails entirely at oshb:Ps.51.14 (tier=none) -- the verse the sentence structure attaches it to.

challenges.claim: observed_substrate_signals claims תְּ֝כַבְּסֵ֗נִי at 51:9 'repeats the wash-root of oshb:Ps.51.4's' הֶ֭רֶב, but הֶ֭רֶב is not the wash-root.
challenges.evidence: As in LF-145-1: הֶ֭רֶב is from r-b-h ('increase/greatly'), a different root from k-b-s, the actual wash-root of both כַּבְּסֵ֣נִי at 51:4 and תְּ֝כַבְּסֵ֗נִי at 51:9. The cross-row recurrence claimed is real (k-b-s does recur across the 51:4|51:9 seam) but the row names the wrong word as its source.

challenges.claim: "the strongest of the psalm's 4 internal seams (sweep: 4 row boundaries)" miscounts the psalm's own row set, or names its count-object ambiguously.
challenges.evidence: freeze/cluster_map.json confirms Psalm 51 has exactly 4 rows total (145-148, tiling 51:1-19 exactly with no gap or overlap per check_tiling.py), which yields 3 internal seams between them (145|146, 146|147, 147|148), not 4. 'Internal seams' and 'row boundaries' are used as though interchangeable in the same clause without specifying whether the psalm's own opening threshold (title|51:1) is being counted as a fourth 'seam' -- the count-object is not named precisely enough to verify which reading is intended.

reviews.reasoning: אֲלַמְּדָ֣ה (MT 51:15 = web:Ps.51.13) is a genuine 1cs Piel cohortative ('let me teach'), correctly identified as a register shift away from the imperative cluster before it -- no morphological error found. All WEB quotes verified verbatim against source. The seam at 51:12|51:13 (imperative cluster to cohortative vow) and the seam at 51:17|51:18 (sacrifice-theology conclusion to Zion petition, itself flagged next door as a debated seam) are both real, independently checkable register shifts. Confidence medium is appropriate given the next row's own disclosed uncertainty about whether 51:16-17 belongs with 51:18-19 instead. No defects found.

The span is the psalm's final two verses and tiles exactly against 51:1-19 alongside the other three rows in this psalm, with no gap. The underlying hapax claim survives independent review -- I reread all of 51:1-19 and confirmed Zion/Jerusalem language occurs nowhere else in the psalm -- but the row's own quoted Hebrew evidence for that claim is wrong (see LF-148-1). The row already discloses this seam as the mandated rival/debated register entry and rates itself medium_low; the correction below replaces a wrong citation with the right one for the same conclusion, and does not overturn the row's own honest uncertainty.

challenges.claim: Both the rationale and observed_substrate_signals gloss צִיּ֑וֹן תִּ֝בְנֶ֗ה as 'the walls of Jerusalem' -- it does not mean that.
challenges.evidence: MT 51:20 (oshb:Ps.51.20) reads heitivah birtzoncha et צִיּ֑וֹן תִּ֝בְנֶ֗ה חוֹמ֥וֹת יְרוּשָׁלִָֽם. צִיּ֑וֹן תִּ֝בְנֶ֗ה = 'Zion... you will build' (Zion is the object of 'do well to'; the verb 'you will build' takes its own object next); the actual Hebrew for 'the walls of Jerusalem' is the following, unquoted, two words in the same verse, חוֹמ֥וֹת יְרוּשָׁלִָֽם. collate.py confirms both phrases genuinely occur at oshb:Ps.51.20 (byte tier), so this is a same-verse quote/gloss swap, not a wrong-verse citation -- but since this pairing is the row's sole quoted evidence for its topographic register-shift argument, the argument's textual anchor is currently the wrong two words.
